app.tagline: Tune-up for Windows. Every change can be undone.
banner.readOnly: PitCrew is not running as administrator, so you can look but not change anything. Close it and open it again, answering Yes on the Windows prompt.
banner.otherUser: Windows approved administrator rights with a different account than the one signed in. Changes for "your user", cleanup of your files and app removal are blocked, because they would hit that other account.
banner.testMode: Test mode: restore points are turned off. Use this only in Windows Sandbox or a virtual machine.
page.performance.title: Performance
page.performance.intro: Only settings with a real, documented effect. Pick what you want and click Apply; PitCrew creates a restore point first.
page.privacy.title: Privacy
page.privacy.intro: Limit what Windows collects and shows you. Each item links to Microsoft's documentation for that setting.
page.cleanup.title: Cleanup
page.cleanup.intro: See how much space each item takes, then pick what to delete. Deleting can't be undone.
page.apps.title: Built-in apps
page.apps.intro: Remove preinstalled apps you don't use. They are removed only for your user and can be reinstalled from here.
page.drivers.title: Drivers
page.drivers.intro: Driver updates published on Windows Update. PitCrew checks whether each one is really newer than what you have.
page.about.title: About PitCrew
page.about.intro: Open source, no ads, no telemetry of its own.

about.text:
PitCrew is a free, open-source tune-up tool for Windows 10 and 11. Every setting it changes is recorded first, so it can be put back exactly as it was. It only includes settings with a documented, real effect; docs/NOT-INCLUDED.md lists popular tweaks we left out and why.

Translations other than English and Portuguese were machine-generated. Native speakers are welcome to review them.

error.powerPlan: Windows didn't switch to this power plan. Some PCs (those with Modern Standby) only allow the Balanced plan.
page.maintenance.title: Maintenance
page.maintenance.intro: Repairs and checks that Windows can run on its own but hides away. Pick what to run.
page.restore.title: Restore points
page.restore.intro: A restore point is a snapshot of Windows settings, drivers and programs. If something goes wrong, System Restore takes the PC back to it. Your documents are not affected.
page.history.title: History
page.history.intro: Everything PitCrew changed on this PC. Select items and click Undo to put them back exactly as they were.
dialog.apply.title: Review the changes
dialog.apply.noRestorePointNote: Without it, PitCrew's own Undo still works. The restore point is an extra safety net for the whole system.
dialog.apply.testMode: Restore points are off in test mode.
restore.empty: No restore points yet. System Protection may be off for the Windows drive; creating one here offers to turn it on.
restore.needsAdmin: Open PitCrew as administrator to see the restore points.
history.empty: PitCrew has not changed anything on this PC yet.
history.removedTweak: No longer in the catalog, so it cannot be undone from here.
history.untrusted: An undo journal with unsafe permissions was set aside and is not used: {0}
maintenance.repair: Check and repair Windows system files
maintenance.repair.detail: Runs DISM (RestoreHealth) and then SFC. Fixes damaged Windows files that cause crashes and odd errors. Takes 10 to 40 minutes and downloads repair files from Windows Update if needed.
maintenance.componentCleanup.detail: DISM StartComponentCleanup: deletes superseded versions of updated system files. Updates installed so far can still be uninstalled.
maintenance.diskHealth.detail: Reads what each drive reports about itself (health, wear, temperature, errors). Changes nothing.
maintenance.driverBackup.detail: Copies every driver not included with Windows to a folder in Documents. Handy before reinstalling Windows. Can take more than 1 GB with graphics drivers.
maintenance.confirmLong: "{0}" can take 10 to 40 minutes, and PitCrew stays busy until it finishes. Continue?
maintenance.confirmDriverBackup: Save a copy of every third-party driver to {0}? It can take more than 1 GB.
maintenance.repairFixed: System files: problems were found and repaired. Restart the PC.
maintenance.repairFailed: System files: some problems could not be repaired. Details in C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log.
disk.Unhealthy: FAILING, back up your files now
cleanup.wu-cache.detail: Update files already installed. Windows downloads them again if it ever needs them. Skipped while an update waits for a restart.
cleanup.delivery-optimization.detail: Copies of updates kept to share with other PCs. Safe to delete.
cleanup.error-reports.detail: Crash reports already sent to (or kept for) Microsoft.
cleanup.minidumps.detail: Small files Windows writes after a blue screen. Keep them if you are investigating crashes.
cleanup.rebootPending: Waiting for a restart to finish updates
drivers.board: Motherboard: {0} {1}. Drivers and BIOS from the maker: {2}
page.explorer.title: Explorer & taskbar
page.explorer.intro: Small changes to File Explorer, the taskbar and the Start menu. Mostly a matter of taste; each one says what changes.

msg.restorePolicyBlocked: System Restore is turned off by a policy (set by your organization or by another tool). PitCrew does not override it, so it cannot create restore points here.

page.startup.intro: Turning an app off here works exactly like Task Manager: it stops opening with Windows, nothing is deleted, and you can turn it back on any time.
page.startup.title: Startup apps

error.dataUntrusted: PitCrew's data folder (%ProgramData%\PitCrew) isn't protected, so it won't change anything this session. Open PitCrew again as administrator; if this message stays, check that folder's permissions.
